Each test starts from a clean database.

terms.meaning: The test runner that executes these checks.
A temporary database held in computer memory that disappears when the test ends.

sections.name: File setup, caseParams, anchorParams
sections.title: Test setup and helpers
sections.what: Loads the test tools, the route handlers, and the services. Defines two small helpers that wrap case and anchor ids in the form the route handlers expect.
sections.why: Likely reason: route handlers receive their parameters as a promise, so the helpers rebuild that shape for each call.
sections.watch_out: If the helper shape stops matching what the routes expect, every test fails at once.

sections.name: Anchor & Verifier API Routes (part 1)
sections.title: Creation and listing tests
sections.what: Before each test it resets to a clean demo database. The tests check that an anchor can be created and listed, and that an empty request is rejected.
sections.why: Each test needs a known starting point. Reason not stated in the code beyond the setup and cleanup.
sections.watch_out: The cleanup after each test prevents leftover anchors from affecting later tests.

sections.name: Anchor & Verifier API Routes (part 2)
sections.title: Missing result and public verification tests
sections.what: Checks that a missing result returns 404, a valid anchor verifies with matching fingerprints, and an unknown anchor id returns 404.
sections.why: Checks the core promise that an unchanged result verifies and a changed or unknown one does not.
sections.watch_out: The expected signer and case reference strings are fixed, so changing them in the code breaks this test.

summary: Automated tests that check creating, listing, validating, and publicly verifying anchors work together.
purpose: Confirms the anchor flow still works after changes.
why: Likely reason: catches breakage in the anchor feature before users see it.
how: Before each test, the file creates a fresh in-memory database and loads demo case data with verification run. Each test then creates an anchor, lists anchors, sends bad input, checks public verification, and checks unknown ids. After each test the database is reset.
inputs: Demo case ids and result ids from the synthetic seed data.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each test.
risks: Tests rely on the demo seed data. If seed values change, tests can fail even when the code is correct. Expected signer names are fixed strings.
debug: Run this test file alone and read the first failing expectation. Then check the seed data for the case named in the failure.
